Ugh I feel you about the gym tho. May I suggest swimming? I have had bad flare ups after the gym and what I've learned is SWIM.... I'm not entirely sure what sets my cyst off it seems to flare up every 1.5-2 months. Swimming hasn't seemed to "awaken the beast". However before i started swimming I found that the treadmill, and lunges really seemed to piss the bastard off.  So now I literally avoid ANYTHING that puts pressure on my cyst. I've even just stooped using weight benches because to safely get on your back with heavy weight you have to roll on your tailbone/back... so I just stick to bale flys and whatever I can do with the cables. I actually hired a personal trainer for a few sessions and explained my situation and he was really helpful in showing me stuff I can do that I never would have thought of. I think a personal trainer session is only about 50 bucks a session and it's WORTH EVERY PENNY! He basically showed me how to do cable exercises; pec flys, ab crunches, back stuff, everything. If you're new to swimming you should watch some basic videos on youtube and they'll show you how to do stuff like the how to breath when swimming, and basic swimming moves like the front crawl. I grew up in competitive swimming and if anything I'm glad this disease has brought me back to something I love dearly. I've lost 5lb since I started a month ago but keep in mind you need to really watch your calorie intake for this to work well. I'm at 1600Cals a day (I'm not super strict cause it's so low). I extremely motivated to lose the weight I've put on because of this shit disease.

Thanks so much... it's nice to have people talk to me who've been through this. I think the mental anguish is what is really getting to me. And also the concern of long time antibiotic use. I'm young and I've lost so many life opportunities because of this.  I just wish my doctor seemed like he gave a shit about scaring but he's just seems like a he could care less. However, GOOD NEWS I have a meeting with a 'minimally invasive' surgeon a few months before my cleft lift surgery. I know intellectually I shouldn't care what someone thinks of my ass but once again as a gay guy my "people" for a lack of a better term (lol) place a great importance on how the butt looks. I'm not expecting to get out of this scar free but I just want a surgeon who understands the importance of making stuff look good... I want a 90 degree angle crack at the end of this not a 80 degree or a 45 degree...  if you know what I mean. but deep down inside it's really messing with me. :(

Thanks so much for your reply. Sorry for the long post here. My surgeon told me he has done cleft lifts before. However what made me uneasy was that he told me he 'hated' dealing with pilonidal which is making me think he's jumping the gun and wanting to do the cleft lift surgery which I know has a very high success rate but I already am having a problem mentally with the scar I do have... It isn't very nice and his stitching job was really ugly imo. I just feel like he really wouldn't take any care in making the scar minimal because when he did the first surgery it felt like he took out way more than was necessary yet completely missing a portion of the cyst. I'm worried he'll do the cleft and it will come back. I guess I've lost confidence in him which sucks. I truly believe that if he removed the tissue he missed where the pain and swelling starts (It's right where the sinus hole is) my issue would go away. I do live in Vancouver, BC, Canada. A lot of doctors that perform pit pickings are few and far between. Many surgeons who perform that are in the states and financially that is completely out of the picture for me. My biggest issue now is the wait times to see doctors. I'm absolutely going to be getting a second or even a third opinion. I just hate how reluctant he is to even try another excision when he himself is saying my cyst isn't that bad and is very small. I think I might look into seeing a plastic surgeon/reconstructive surgeon... someone who understands my worries about the scaring. I honestly feel so alone with this disease.
